story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The Blues have won three straight, while the Oilers (17-5-3) lost 7-4 to Carolina last night. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (tied for second in the NHL) and the Blues sixth in the Central (tied for 17th).

The Oilers’ record (.740) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.536), largely thanks to their finishing. The Blues’ record (.565) is about what their chances are worth. If the Oilers’ record were closer to their chances, like the Blues’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd) and get their defensemen shooting (4th). Edmonton has scored 3.84 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Blues, they keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd). They also get some of the league’s best looks (3rd), so the Blues wait for good looks, but the Oilers settle for hopeful ones.

Connor McDavid (13 G / 44 A / 57 P in 25 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in nine straight games against St. Louis. Leon Draisaitl (22 G / 24 A / 46 P in 25 GP) has a team-high 22 goals, the most in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (5 G / 18 A / 23 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Edmonton. Jimmy Snuggerud (13 G / 5 A / 18 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, tied for tenth in the NHL.
Tristan Jarry (6-1-3 / .909 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to go for Edmonton. Joel Hofer (9-6-1 / .923 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for St. Louis and is expected to start.
